mainProgression.description: Classical chromatic descending bassline in A minor (A → G → F# → F → E) alternating with explosive hard-rock power chords.

sectionProgressions.description: Intricate PIMA fingerpicked arpeggios over a chromatic descending bassline
Thunderous distorted full-band crashes under Robert Plant's soaring cries

harmonicFunction: Am/G (i4/2) - First stepwise bass drop (A → G) maintaining minor suspense
Am/F# (i6) - Dorian major-sixth chord (F#) creating poignant flamenco-like coloration
F (VI) - Dark submediant resolving the chromatic descent
E7 (V7) - Classical major dominant containing the G# leading tone pulling decisively back into Am

techniques.name: Flamenco-Style Fingerpicking & Dynamic Light/Shade Explosions
techniques.description: Combining classical thumb-and-finger PIMA arpeggio rolls on steel-string acoustic with sudden explosive transitions into cranked electric power chords

notes: Bass walkdown: Open A string → 3rd fret low E (G) → 2nd fret low E (F#) → 1st fret low E (F) → open low E
Upper voices: Ringing C, E, and A triad notes on strings 2, 3, and 4
Flamenco-style rasgueado acoustic strums and rapid pick transitions
sequence: Roll upward through strings 4, 3, and 2 with index (I), middle (M), and ring (A)
Maintain smooth chromatic bass descent without stopping upper voice arpeggios
Slam into the heavy electric section with violent downstrokes
tips: Jimmy Page played his 1968 Gibson J-200 acoustic, using light and shade dynamics ('dramatically loud and dramatically soft')
Use thumb over the neck to fret the 1st fret F and 2nd fret F# notes on the low E string
The electric crunch was a 1959 Telecaster through a cranked Supro amplifier

sections.name: Fingerpicked Chromatic Descent
sections.description: Page's legendary acoustic fingerpicking masterclass opening Led Zeppelin's debut album side one.
notes: Let upper chord voices ring continuously
Accentuate the chromatic bassline (A → G → F# → F → E)

sections.name: Heavy Electric Explosion
sections.description: The sudden eruption of full-band distorted rock power on 'Baby, baby, I wanna leave you!'.
notes: Massive dynamic jump from delicate acoustic to roaring electric
Lock tight with John Bonham's thunderous bass drum

guitar.pickup: Under-saddle acoustic mic; Bridge single-coil on Telecaster

amp.recommended: Supro 1624T Dual Tone 1x12 Tube Combo & Marshall Plexi

effects.distortion: Sola Sound Tone Bender MKII Fuzz (for electric explosions)

beginner.title: Chord Shapes & Chromatic Bass
steps: Learn the five chord shapes: Am, Am/G, Am/F#, F, and E7
Practice the chromatic bass walkdown on strings 5 and 6 at 50 BPM

intermediate.title: PIMA Fingerpicking Arpeggios
steps: Master the thumb-index-middle-ring fingerpicking cycle cleanly
Execute the chromatic bass shift without interrupting upper chord sustain
Play along with the studio track at 68 BPM

advanced.title: Extreme Dynamic Contrast
steps: Transition seamlessly between delicate folk fingerpicking and violent rock power chords
Incorporate flamenco-inspired rasgueado strums before the electric drops
Capture Jimmy Page's definitive 'light and shade' studio production live

commonMistakes: Letting upper strings mute during the thumb fretting on F and F#
Rushing the tempo during the acoustic fingerpicking sections
Failing to make the electric explosion dramatically louder than the acoustic verse
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Chromatic bass walkdown isolation drill
10 minutes: PIMA fingerpicking pattern at 55 BPM → 68 BPM with metronome
5 minutes: Heavy electric chord transition timing
focusAreas: Thumb-over fretting clarity on strings 5 and 6
metronomeWork: Keep metronome at 68 BPM with steady eighth-note subdivision
